items.title: UX playground: compose components in a layout
items.description: A space of the documentation site where UX designers combine the coded components in a layout, like FigJam, before a prototype or development.
items.why: Today, testing a combination of components means writing a prototype in code. UX designers need a quick way to explore an idea on their own, with real components, before it becomes a prototype or goes to development.
items.scope: Included: only the coded components (@ds/components) and the tokens, so every composition can be built as is; a composition can be the starting point of a prototype ticket; a missing component found while composing is a signal for the backlog. Different from the playground.tsx of each component (one component, its props): here several components are combined. Decisions asked first: how to compose (free canvas like FigJam, the design system grid 4 / 8 / 12 columns, or a canvas with layout frames); whether the variants, states and texts of each placed component can be changed; how compositions are saved (not saved, in the browser, or in the repository and shared); whether a composition can become a prototype ticket; annotations (sticky notes, comments); where it sits in the navigation (a new space next to Prototypes, or a page under Prototypes).

items.title: Git workflow: project branches for long pieces of work
items.description: A new branch type, project/<name>, for long pieces of work on the documentation site, each with its own conversation.
items.why: Governance branches are very short and merged as soon as a step is approved; a large piece of work like the UX playground (B130) needs its own long branch, merged once it is validated.
items.scope: Included: the project/<name> branch type (kebab-case, long lifetime, merged into develop once the project is validated or on request) and its conversation Projet <Name>, archived at the end, in git-workflow, CLAUDE.md and the Git workflow page of the site; then governance/ux-playground renamed project/ux-playground and B130 updated. Not included: the work of the UX playground itself (B130).

items.title: Documentation site: accessibility follow-up
items.description: Markdown code blocks and tables inside cards stay readable; the brand fill of a checked control is checked for contrast.
items.why: Found by the full compliance audit before the merge into develop (audits/2026-10-30-before-develop-merge.md), and by the audit of Step B039-1 for finding 47 (audits/2026-11-04-B039-1.md).
items.scope: Audit findings 42 and 43: Markdown code blocks of the Skills and Agents cards (and any Markdown) overflow the card; the pair background.brand on background.page (checkbox fill, pressed toggle) is not in tokens/contrast-pairs.json. Audit finding 47: tables inside a Card (Markdown tables and table.tokens on the How to use skills, Agents and Release planning pages) inherit overflow-wrap: anywhere from .ds-card-text, so the first column shrinks to about one character and words break in two. Decisions asked first: same look as pre.code (surface background, padding) or scroll only; background.brand or border.focus for a checked control fill; tables in cards fixed on the site only (docs.css) or in the Card component (complete: new version and changelog); too-wide tables scroll horizontally or wrap between words. Extended on 2026-11-15 (Design System Lead, R2 release review, audits/2026-11-15-R2.md): finding 64, the search field border on the header (border.strong on background.brand-subtle, measured 3.19:1) is not in tokens/contrast-pairs.json; finding 65, the accessible name of the Portfolio skills panel ("Skills, tools and expertise", PortfolioPage.tsx) no longer names the Languages group. Decisions asked first: list the pair in contrast-pairs.json or change the field or header colors; the wording of the panel name.
doneWhen: Long code lines in Markdown scroll inside their block and never overflow the card.
The brand fill pair is in contrast-pairs.json and npm run tokens passes.
Tables inside cards keep whole words and never break a word in two.
The search field border pair is in contrast-pairs.json (or the colors are changed) and npm run tokens passes.
The accessible name of the Portfolio skills panel covers every group, Languages included.
The next compliance audit no longer lists findings 42, 43, 47, 64 and 65.

items.title: Link: code labels and spacing in lists
items.description: Links whose label is code, and standalone links in lists and tables, follow the Link guidelines.
items.why: Found by the compliance audit of Step B018-4 (audits/2026-11-05-B018-4.md), once the documentation site adopted the Link.
items.scope: Audit finding 51: the skill tree links (How to use skills) have a <code> label on background.subtle, a background not in the Link guidelines nor in contrast-pairs.json (the contrast passes: 5.50:1 to 9.56:1), and the code style replaces the surrounding text style. Audit finding 52: standalone links in the skill tree list (8px apart) and in the Branches and Changelog tables (16px apart) are closer than the 24px of the Link guidelines, while WCAG 2.5.8 (24px between target centers) passes. Decisions asked first: may a link label contain code (then add the text.link* on background.subtle pairs and allow that background), or drop <code> inside links; does the 24px rule mean the gap or the WCAG center distance (rewrite the guidelines wording), or apply 24px in lists and tables.
doneWhen: The Link guidelines say whether a link label may contain code, and the site follows it.
The Link guidelines state the 24px rule unambiguously, and the lists and tables of the site follow it.
Any new contrast pair is in contrast-pairs.json and npm run tokens passes.
The next compliance audit no longer lists findings 51 and 52.

items.why: Building block of the Canvas (B142): the UX playground canvas has visible zoom controls, a group reused as one unit, so it is its own component, completed before the Canvas code (component-structure).
items.scope: Design, guidelines and code of the ZoomControls component, each stage approved by the Design System Lead (component skill), in a Composant ZoomControls conversation on component/ZoomControls. Already decided in the Composant Canvas conversation: a zoom out button, the zoom level in percent, a zoom in button and a fit to screen button; tertiary IconButtons; a container with background surface, radius 8 and shadow.dropdown; placed at the bottom right of the Canvas. The rest of the anatomy, the sizes, states and tokens are decided in the design stage (never-invent).
doneWhen: The ZoomControls design, guidelines and code are approved; meta.json status complete, version 1.0.
The accessibility and token audits pass.
ZoomControls is exported from @ds/components, ready for the Canvas (B142).

items.title: Documentation site: tablet screen size tokens
items.description: The site's simulated tablet screens use the size.viewport-tablet tokens, like mobile and desktop.
items.why: Compliance audit finding 68 (audits/2026-11-19-B143-1.md): the Playground tab and the Prototype preview frames read the tablet width and height from breakpoint.tablet / breakpoint.desktop (media-query tokens), while size.viewport-tablet / size.viewport-tablet-height now exist for a simulated tablet screen (B143).
items.scope: docs/src/PlaygroundTab.tsx (tablet screen size and its comment) and docs/src/pages/PrototypePage.tsx (tablet preview frame): width from size.viewport-tablet, height from size.viewport-tablet-height. Same values (768 × 1024): no visual change.
doneWhen: The site's simulated tablet screens read size.viewport-tablet and size.viewport-tablet-height.
Finding 68 is gone from the next compliance audit.

items.title: Documentation site: component page tabs on small screens
items.description: The tab row of the component pages stays within the page width on mobile and tablet.
items.why: Compliance audit finding 69 (audits/2026-11-21-B143-3.md): the hand-built tab row (display: flex, no wrap, no overflow) needs about 590px on a phone against about 327px; the whole page scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow). Seen in the browser on Button and Frame.
items.scope: docs/src/pages/ComponentPage.tsx (tab row, lines 72-89) and docs/src/docs.css (.tabs, lines 428-440): fix the hand-built tablist now, without waiting for Tabs (B093). Then check the Playground canvas again at mobile width. Decision to ask first: how the row behaves when the tabs do not fit (e.g. horizontal scroll of the row, wrap, or a menu).
doneWhen: On mobile and tablet, the component page tab row stays within the page width and the page does not scroll sideways.
The Playground tab does not overflow the page at mobile width.
Finding 69 is gone from the next compliance audit.
